name: Flaky Test Management Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in flaky test management work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in flaky test management work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When flaky test management guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
2. Measure before optimizing any flaky test management bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. Before starting flaky test management work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
4. Keep flaky test management outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen flaky test management approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. State assumptions about flaky test management explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
7. Prefer explicit, readable flaky test management solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
8. Validate flaky test management outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
9. Check that flaky test management terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of flaky test management correctness.
- Avoid introducing new flaky test management abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not silently drop flaky test management edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting flaky test management assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about flaky test management over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
